read_scope: Complete cleanup_patterns.py initial candidate and every final-source change
Complete scheduler/orchestrator production diff and actual periodic handoff
claim_change_guard, attempt_effect_lock, execution_catalog and native begin lock ownership
Actual shared mode-ro lifecycle opener and current native training/evaluation publication bindings

findings: Candidate enumeration is no-follow and precedes locking; a fresh read-only SQLite snapshot is created only inside the same effect guard used by native claim/begin/reset. All-phase current attempts and agreed task lifecycle are both checked before unlink.

Incomplete effect/stop evidence and retained owners refuse cleanup. The supplied controller Lake is routing input, not an inherited transaction grant; cfg-only native paths discover only existing authority without bootstrap.

Actual main database plus sidecars and launch-bound B1 control roots are protected immediately before unlink, including old control/state identity slots after cfg drift. The independently reproduced artifact-root defect is closed.

Current B2 result publication explicitly inherits source_binding.root in observation_publication.py; it does not choose a separate mutable cfg root. Therefore the training-root protection also covers the current B2 result store. An initial static concern about a separate B2 root was ruled out by reading the actual producer; no test/failure or new requirement is counted.
Configured source/report/control locations and private framework namespaces are not disposable. Ending ** remains directory-only, preserving the old no-file-match semantics.

Final legacy protections resolve model_lineage.artifact and eval_checkpoint relative to the task, and resume.immutable_inputs relative to the project, retaining declared trees. The default best_model.pt is protected when eval_script enables the legacy evaluation path. The change adds declaration metadata only, not file hashing, DB writes or a new authority path.
Success counts follow completed unlink plus directory sync; refusals are observable. This is not atomic multi-file deletion or recovery from arbitrary same-user path races.
review.docs_assessment: The contract correctly excludes standalone GC, cleanup.script execution, cold-storage moves, natural-exit descendant proof and research-efficiency claims. Pattern budgets, directory-only terminal **, legacy declaration bases and directory-tree retention match the final implementation.

No real CPU training/external evaluator execution; no paid provider, holdout, standalone GC or custom script.
No new result-schema absence asserted; public run_cleanup return None retained.
Four behavioral failures are not four independently isolated root causes; shared unsafe legacy deletion loop is exercised across four lifecycle contexts.
